title: Private Runner Config Catalogue (personal)
content:
Purpose:
Small personal catalogue of config shapes and control API ideas for the private/on-prem runner (keeps coming up in calls). Treat as a living scratchpad: not finalized, but intended to converge into a single spec we can hand to infra and platform teams.

Key constraints (reminder):
- Customers may be air-gapped: control plane calls must be optional.
- Mutating operations should be idempotent and resumable (retries, reconciler-friendly).
- Minimal runtime surface on customer infra: prefer a small agent + optional sidecar model.
- Secrets must flow via KMS/HSM or ephemeral bootstrap tokens; never baked into configs.
- Need a model for local vs control-plane driven rollouts (pull vs push).

High-level runner roles (simple taxonomy):
- agent: lightweight process that communicates with customer infra and runs containers/GPUs locally.
- sidecar: colocated proxy handling telemetry, caching, and warmups for processes that speak the Redwood runtime protocol.
- operator: controller (optional, hosted or customer-managed) that coordinates fleet-level policies and certificate distribution.

ASCII topologies (2 variants):
1) Air-gapped private (pull-first):
   [Operator (hosted) --optional--> USB / physical transfer]
   Customer network:
   [Operator seeds bootstrap token] -> (manual transfer) -> [Agent] -> launches runner containers (no outbound).

2) VPC-connected (push/pull mix):
   [Operator] <--- control-plane TLS ----> [Agent] -- unix socket --> [Sidecar] -- grpc --> [LocalRunner]

Proposed control API shape (HTTP/JSON over TLS)  -- minimal verbs: get, apply, status.
- GET /v1/runner/{id}/config  -> returns active config + version metadata
- POST /v1/runner/{id}/apply -> accepts config document; returns operation id for async reconcile
- GET /v1/operation/{op_id} -> operation state (queued/running/succeeded/failed), events log
- POST /v1/runner/{id}/heartbeat -> short stamp to mark liveness (agent->operator)

Example responses (informal):
Request: GET /v1/runner/r-42/config
Response: 200
{
  "runner_id": "r-42",
  "config_version": "2026-02-20-rc3",
  "profiles": ["default-gpu","low-latency-cpu"],
  "applied_at": "2026-02-20T14:12:03Z"
}
(we'll translate to strict JSON schema later)

Agent-side local config (YAML sketch) -- runner-profile is the unit customers tune:
---
runner_id: r-42
node_labels:
  site: "east-1"
profiles:
  default-gpu:
    gpu_count: 4
    max_concurrency: 80
    batch_window_ms: 12
    quant_profile: q8_0
    prewarm_templates:
      - model: 'gpt-medium-v0'
        warmup_tokens: 2560
  low-latency-cpu:
    cpu_shares: 1200
    concurrency: 6
    batching: false
    quant_profile: int8
telemetry:
  sink: sidecar://local
  sampling: 0.01
secrets:
  kms_key_ref: projects/acme/locations/us/keyRings/rw/cryptoKeys/runner-bootstrap
---
Notes on values: prefer explicit fields over magic strings. "profiles" should be named in UI and referenced by rollout policies.

Rollout model ideas (operational):
- Canary by profile subset: apply new profile to 5% of nodes (by label or "test" pool) -> monitor cost/latency/regressions -> widen.
- Fallbacks: each profile must have a fallback model-variant to use when quantization/memory OOM occurs.
- Local override: node admin can pin a profile locally with higher precedence; operator must record override and avoid overwriting unless forced.

Sidecar contract (textual):
- Sidecar exposes two unix sockets: /run/sidecar/control.sock (JSON control) and /run/sidecar/metrics.sock (prometheus-ish values).
- Sidecar is responsible for: batching hints, prefix cache, local telemetry redact, and token-cost accounting.
- Control messages are short and idempotent. Example: {"type":"prefetch","model":"gpt-medium-v0","warmup_tokens":1000} -> ack/accepted.

Example minimal local control message (line-delimited JSON):
{"op":"prefetch","id":"op-9","model":"gpt-medium-v0","until":"2026-03-15T12:00:00Z"}
{ "status":"accepted","op":"op-9","ts":"2026-03-12T15:44:12Z" }

Observability pieces to include in spec:
- Event stream for operations (apply/start/fail/retry) kept for 7d by default in sidecar; operator may request longer retention.
- Per-profile latency p95/p99, tokens-per-second, model-fallback counts, and OOM/reschedule counts.
- Local sample traces (redacted) for failures to speed RCA.

Security/Bootstrap flow (sketch):
1) Customer registers org -> receives org id and a short-lived bootstrap token via UI/download.
2) Agent uses token to request a provisioning cert from operator (if reachable) OR writes token into a sealed file for air-gap manual handoff.
3) Agent rotates node key daily via HSM/KMS if available; otherwise recommends manual rotation cadence.

Open questions (TODOs / discussion points):
- Config size limits: how big can an applied config be? need to set hard limits (e.g., 64KB) to avoid abuse.
- Should we support git-backed configs (repo-as-source-of-truth) for operators that prefer declarative flows? tradeoffs: auditability vs complexity.
- Sidecar API auth model: mTLS to sidecar? unix-socket + local ACL is simpler but less standard.
- How to represent multi-model affinity rules (co-locate model shards vs isolate). I sketched "profiles" but might need a richer affinity DSL.
- Rollback semantics: should apply create an operation that can be cancelled and reversed automatically on failure? probably yes.

Migration notes (for existing Hosted-only customers):
- Provide an import tool to convert hosted route settings -> runner profiles with sensible defaults (batching window heuristics, quantization recommendations).
- Add a compatibility shim so existing SDK customers can point to private runner endpoint with minimal SDK changes (env var + endpoint override).

Next steps (personal checklist):
- [ ] Draft JSON Schema for /v1/runner/{id}/config response (strict types, enums).
- [ ] Prototype minimal sidecar control socket and a tiny shim that accepts prefetch ops (local PoC).
- [ ] Sync with Diego about telemetry retention and legal for sample traces.
- [ ] Run a short customer call script to validate air-gap expectations.

References and quick links (placeholders):
- internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-runner/pull/278
- infra ticket: INFR-4821
- ops note (confluence): Private-Runner-Operator-Notes

Random scribbles / heuristics I keep returning to:
- "profile" should be small, composable, and nameable. Customers think in names.
- Keep local overrides explicit and visible in UI (audit trail).
- Avoid long-running blocking apply flows; return an operation id and let reconciler finish work.

End of notebook entry (long—will split into formal spec later).
